🔊 Iran–US MoU negotiated with maximum national interests fully safeguarded: Gharibabadi

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs, Kazem Gharibabadi, says the recent Iran–US memorandum of understanding was achieved under conditions of complete distrust, emphasizing that safeguarding maximum national interests remained the guiding principle of the Iranian negotiating team.

Speaking in a televised interview on Monday, Gharibabadi stressed that the agreement reflects Iran’s leverage derived from its military and diplomatic strength, noting that bringing the adversary to the negotiating table is itself the result of Iranians’ power.
​
The diplomat explained that the memorandum was finalized after extensive negotiations involving indirect mediation by Pakistan and Qatar, with additional facilitation from Switzerland for the formal signing process. He said the text was subject to long and meticulous discussions, during which Iran insisted on incorporating all its final revisions, many of which were ultimately accepted. The deputy minister confirmed that the signing ceremony is scheduled for Friday, after which implementation mechanisms will gradually begin.
​
He underlined that Iran’s commitments under the MoU are strictly conditional and reciprocal. Iran’s measures will be fully aligned with the level of compliance shown by the other side, he said, adding that Tehran will closely monitor implementation and respond proportionally to any violation or failure by the United States. According to him, a 60-day negotiation period will follow the signing, focusing exclusively on the nuclear file and the lifting of sanctions, including unilateral, secondary, and international restrictions.
​
Gharibabadi further stated that Iran’s negotiating position was anchored in both diplomatic and military deterrence. He noted that recent regional developments and responses by Iranian Armed Forces contributed to accelerating the negotiation process and shaping the final text. Without military strength and national unity, this outcome would not have been possible, he said.
​
He also confirmed that the implementation of initial US obligations, such as ending restrictions, ending hostilities, and releasing blocked Iranian assets, will be verified before Iran fully enters the next negotiation phase. Only after such verification, he said, will Tehran proceed with structured talks under the agreed framework.
​
Concluding his remarks, Gharibabadi reiterated that Iran’s approach combines diplomacy with readiness for defense, stressing that even with agreements in place, the country remains fully prepared to counter any future threats.

📡 Pakistan says it supports ‘every endeavour’ to consolidate US-Iran memorandum of understanding

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Pakistan’s Foreign Minister and Deputy Prime Minister Muhammad Ishaq Dar says his country “warmly welcomes” a memorandum of understanding (MoU) reached between Iran and the United States to permanently end the war, emphasizing that Islamabad is ready to support efforts to consolidate the understanding.

Ishaq Dar made the remarks on Monday in a post on X after the US and Iran announced an agreement on the memorandum of understanding following negotiations facilitated by Pakistan. The talks, which began in early April, resulted in a temporary ceasefire that halted 40 days of war waged by the US and Israel against Iran.
​
“This significant breakthrough reflects the power of sustained diplomatic engagement and the collective resolve of friendly nations to choose dialogue over confrontation,” Pakistan’s foreign minister said.
​
He added that the MoU also “sends a reassuring message to the international community and provides much-needed confidence and stability to global markets and the world economy, particularly for developing countries that are most vulnerable to regional instability.”
​
“Throughout this period, Pakistan remained actively engaged with all concerned parties and consistently advocated restraint and constructive engagement, maintaining that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable means for the resolution of all issues,” Ishaq Dar noted.
​
He appreciated the US and Iran for placing their trust in Pakistan, and praised the diplomatic efforts of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Turkey, Egypt, and others that helped secure the MoU.
​
“As negotiations continue on the outstanding matters, Pakistan stands ready to support every endeavour aimed at consolidating this progress,” Ishaq Dar said.
​
He concluded his post by saying that Pakistan looks forward to “the formal signing ceremony on 19 June in Geneva and remain confident that this positive development will pave the way for enduring peace, stability and shared prosperity for the region and beyond, InshaAllah.”
